subject: Taking data from the list output of a API call

messages.author: 0d5c994b344af3a8
messages.subject: Taking data from the list output of a API call
parts:
Hello - There is a CRAN package (walkscoreAPI) which has a function to perform the API calls associated with the Walk Score website (www.walkscore.com) within the R. 

The function getWS takes longitude, latitude, and a api key and returns a list. 

a <- getWS(-122.3805, 47.67518, "my_api_key") 
> str(a)
List of 6
 $ status     : num 1
 $ walkscore  : num 85
 $ description: chr "Very Walkable"
 $ updated    : chr "2016-04-04 19:48:18.884640"
 $ snappedLong: num -122
 $ snappedLat : num 47.7
 - attr(*, "class")= chr "WalkScore"

I am interested in the second element of "a" and I can get that by typing a[[2]]. 

I now want to do the above for my entire collection of latitudes and longitudes which are in a data frame. I tried 

df$ws <- getWS(df$long, df$lat, "my_api_key")[[2]]

However, I get the error 
Error in file(file, "r") : invalid 'description' argument
In addition: Warning message:
In if (file == "") file <- stdin() else { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Any ideas how I should deal with this? 

Thanks so much.

messages.author: 3355b78f830c2044
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Taking data from the list output of a API call
parts:
Hi Gouri,

Thanks for sharing the walkscoreAPI package - that could be very useful for my research, too.

Without seeing more of your code and what getWS returns, my guess is you would want to call unlist() on the list created by getWS(). You could then retrieve the walkscores associated with your lat/long in the second column of the resulting dataframe.

Hope that helps,
Calvin

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Taking data from the list output of a API call
parts:
Hi,

Calvin is correct - the issue is that the function only takes a single lat/long pair at a time. You can solve this by looping over your lat/long pairs. 

One thing you need to check is your allowed calls to the API per day and per min/hour. Many APIs limit how many and how quickly you can query them. Depending on your network latency, you might exceed the limits and get your API key/IP blocked. Check the terms of the API so you don't potentially block the campus IP from the API. You can slow down your requests if needed by using Sys.sleep().

Lastly, scanning over the source code, the walkscoreAPI package has a pretty poor implementation and WILL break in some situations. You should wrap your call to the API with try() to avoid this from breaking your whole loop.

If the problems with the walkscoreAPI package are cropping up a lot, it would be simple to write your own function to query the API that would be much more robust. 

Matt

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Taking data from the list output of a API call
parts:
Sure - Duncan could probably do much better than I, but here is a stab at it.

You can look at the function call if you type in its name without the parentheses. Walking through the function:

getWS
function (x, y, key) 
{
    URL <- paste("http://api.walkscore.com/score?lat=", y, "&lon=", 
        x, "&wsapikey=", key, sep = "")
    X <- character(0)
    X <- c(X, scan(file = URL, what = "", sep = "\n", quiet = TRUE))
...

At the head of the function, they do not have any checks in place to make sure the input is in the correct format and they use scan(), which does not ensure a valid request is constructed. Better would be to use a function like getForm().

Next,

...   
    string <- X[grep("<walkscore>", X)]
    string2 <- X[grep("<description>", X)]
    string3 <- X[grep("<updated>", X)]
...

The API returns XML by default. They are parsing this themselves, rather than use existing functions that know how to read XML.

Next (and probably the worst),

 if (status == 1) {
        walk <- strsplit(string, "<walkscore>")
        walk2 <- gsub("</walkscore>", "", walk[[1]][2])
        wscore <- as.numeric(walk2)
        ... 
   }
    else {
        wscore <- "NA"
        descr <- "NA"
        ...
    }

The API returns a lot of information about why a request did not return results via the status codes, but all this information is thrown out and NAs are returned. There is nothing more maddening than making a call to an API and getting unexpected results with no explanation. It would be best to preserve this information so the user can diagnose errors.

An example of how it could be done better would be something like this (Note: I requested JSON rather than XML so I can use the fromJSON function. Warning: I am just throwing this together and have not tested it.)

require(RCurl)
require(jsonlite)

getWS <- function(x, y, key)
{
    if(!(is.numeric(x) & is.numeric(y)))
        stop("Lat/Long must be in decimal degrees.")
    
    doc <- getForm("http://api.walkscore.com/score?",
                   format = "json", lat = y, lon = x,
                   wsapikey = key)

    fromJSON(doc)
}

If you wanted to get really fancy, you could have the function return the meaning of the error codes as well, as found at the bottom of https://www.walkscore.com/professional/api.php.

Let me know if you have any questions,

Matt
